# CHM13v2.0 chromosome 1 browser benchmark

**Note:** This file was generated by ChatGPT 5.6 Sol under the direction of Adam Phillippy.

> **Historical artifact:** This records pre-hardening design evidence and does not define the current production method. See `docs/SCIENTIFIC_SPEC.md` and ADR 0004.

Date: 2026-08-28

## Input provenance

* Record: NCBI RefSeq `NC_060925.1`, T2T-CHM13v2.0 chromosome 1
* Length: 248,387,328 bases
* Source: NCBI sequence viewer FASTA endpoint
* Uncompressed FASTA SHA-256:
  `8471eac90037b6886d110288712bb46b2af620e47965a672a7d1555ba0e36c4f`
* The FASTA was held in temporary storage and is not part of the repository.

## Configuration

* Self comparison
* Matrix resolution: 1000
* K-mer length: 21
* Fixed registers: 1024
* HLL precision: 12
* Retained comparison bits: 14
* Tile size: 256 by 256
* Release-optimized Wasm served by the Vite development server
* Headless Google Chrome 152.0.7977.64
* Apple M5 Pro MacBook Pro, 18 CPU cores, 48 GB RAM

## Result

| Milestone | Wall time after file selection |
| --- | ---: |
| FASTA parsed and record selector populated | 2.21 s |
| First overview band reported | 5.80 s |
| Refined 1000 by 1000 overview complete | 6.71 s |

After diagonal-cell and off-diagonal tile symmetry were enabled, the same test gave:

| Milestone | Optimized wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| FASTA parsed and record selector populated | 2.06 s |
| First overview band reported | 5.64 s |
| Refined 1000 by 1000 overview complete | 6.09 s |

After chunked signature construction, real progress reporting, and the UI sprint were
integrated, a full regression run gave:

| Milestone | Current wall time |
| --- | ---: |
| FASTA parsed and record selector populated | 2.07 s |
| Overview signatures complete | 5.15 s |
| First preview tile requested | 5.17 s |
| Refined 1000 by 1000 overview complete | 5.65 s |

The worker reported 4.5 seconds for signature construction plus preview/refined matrix
work after parsing. The browser produced an 853 by 853 WebGL canvas and no page,
worker, or console errors. The optimized worker reported 4.0 seconds. Instrumented
builds retained about 143.9 MiB of Rust/Wasm state. That estimate includes packed sequence,
overview registers, cardinality sidecars, and encoded signatures; it excludes peak
temporaries, allocator metadata, JavaScript transfer buffers, and GPU textures.

The current UI reports approximately 155.3 MiB after completion. Its scope is broader:
it combines the Rust/Wasm estimate with retained JavaScript tile buffers and estimated
GPU texture storage. It is therefore useful as an in-session application tally, but is
not directly comparable to the earlier Wasm-only number or to browser process RSS.

## Interpretation

This is one warm local engineering measurement, not a release acceptance result. It
does establish that the current implementation handles a complete human chromosome
without storing all k-mer hashes and that the original 5 to 15 second planning range
was reasonable on this machine. Repeated runs, cold-cache runs, Firefox/Safari runs,
peak-memory instrumentation, pairwise chromosomes, and lower-spec reference hardware
remain required.
